  "important_model_behaviors": "H1 update — Supported with refinement by observed measurements. V2 remains more responsive, with a shallower high-ratio continuation. Increasing load from 50 to 150 µl lowers V1 by approximately 1.13–1.21 ml at every measured matched ratio: 2/1, 5/1, 10/1 and 50/1. The corresponding V2 increase grows from about 0.13 ml at 2/1 to 2.39 ml at 50/1. This supports a local ratio/loading interaction and weakens complete separability.

H2 update — Partially supported locally. At m160 2/1, increasing load from 50 to 150 µl changes measured V1/V2 from 14.142/34.067 (b21061720e23b7a5bdcb) to 11.517/33.075 (36d971e3231c54486d05). At m90 5/1, the corresponding change is 37.800/67.900 (29db30571b2a1ae59cc7) to 27.475/65.408 (b51b5dbcd2a38b174973). Unlike m167, these V2 values decrease with loading. A global positive loading correction remains unsupported; experimental variability remains an alternative explanation for individual contrasts.

H3 update — Supported as heterogeneous local error structure. m160 has small V2 premeasurement errors at 2/1 despite its earlier 52.81 ml underprediction at 5/1. m216 was overpredicted by 11.63/10.36 ml at 5/1 (33ffc69a253a89f15995), whereas its earlier 10/1 prediction missed by -27.69/-41.93 ml (e47aebe2660b9e1528de). New large underpredictions for m212 and m146 coexist with overprediction for m211. These residuals come from successive model versions, so they are not one current residual surface. Broad polar-group or basic-nitrogen offsets remain inappropriate.

H5 update — The difficult m125 regime is supported, but a pervasive large loading effect is weakened. At 5/1 with 300 µl loading-solvent volume, measured 100 and 150 µl loads give similar endpoints: 42.958/73.100 (74cf50c6ec476a394b01) and 42.267/74.042 (549daca56bed1c9d2bcc). The striking 2/1 contrast changes both load and solvent volume: 100/300 µl gives 15.408/29.583 (c8d43713db33bf820a1d), while 150/500 µl gives 32.950/69.808 (facbcedbecb46072b04c). Observed ID 69f9cefb952abd22672c is actually m101 at 20/1, so the extra m125 contrast described in memory was not completed.

H6 update — Retained within its measured scope. The shallow m147 response remains a counterexample to universal V2 amplification. Additional familiar-grid measurements need a specific unresolved question.

H4 update — The historical m13/m80 reversal premise remains rejected: their measured endpoints and recorded premeasurement predictions are ordered. Separately, current candidate 02ddeed8a16d3adf3e28 predicts V1/V2 of 6.198/5.086 ml, a genuine prediction crossing. This current diagnostic does not establish a measured ordering defect or validate the old rationale.

Current prediction diagnostic — Predictions near newly measured tail conditions move toward their labels. m160 at 5/1 and 50 µl predicts 40.756/98.255 ml, near the measured 100 µl result 40.583/98.392. m216 at 10/1 and 100 µl predicts 53.438/92.852, near the measured 50 µl result 53.417/92.933. These indicate local adjustment, not independent predictive improvement.

Current prediction diagnostic — Loading responses are frequently almost flat. The two missing m125 2/1 factorial corners predict approximately 23.1/47.5 ml despite different amount/solvent-volume combinations. Their near equality is informative because the measured diagonal corners differ substantially. Similar flat predictions recur throughout the supplied pool.

Quantile diagnostic — V1 q10 repeatedly equals zero, making nominal V1 width largely track endpoint scale. Quantiles also cross: candidate 9c06d41471b0bc70e4c7 has V2 q10 10.223 above q90 10.102 and a negative nominal width. Other medians exceed q90. These fields do not support calibrated uncertainty ranking as supplied.",
  "possible_learning_bottlenecks": "Inference from measurements and predictions: response shape between measured conditions may now be more limiting than recognizing an already labeled high endpoint. Measured historical evidence: large V2 misses extend beyond m160/m216. m92 at 50/1 missed by -32.64 ml (7b42519983cf93dd7efd), m212 at 10/1 by -32.70 ml (70cba7a21b5a01fb8e73), and m146 at 10/1 by -28.32 ml (9e3ce3497298084abd83). ML hypothesis: weak use of loading features is plausible, especially for V1. Matched measurements can expose this even when predictions barely change. The evidence does not identify whether representation, regularization, sparse contrasts or unrecorded experimental factors are responsible.

Observed variability: identical recorded inputs sometimes have materially different labels. The m174 records at 30/1, 50 µl and 200 µl PE loading solvent, 704ba630f25fe7f20166 and 92bac523bed1042d6a75, differ by about 4.68 ml on V1 and 5.93 ml on V2. The pool includes familiar low-volume halogenated/nonpolar and ester/carbonyl families, alongside unmeasured molecules such as m107, m37, m47, m117, m116, m129, m191, m205 and m206. Novelty is more useful when attached to an interpretable family or condition comparison.
